title: Principal intrinsic fiber and its specified chain unit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and any scheme $W$. Use the completed module category and the ordered principal tensor tower $V(P)_n=P\otimes_{R_W}[R_W\xrightarrow{t^{n+1}}R_W]$, with transitions $1_P\otimes(t,1)$, of [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers]. Regard this tower degreewise as a complex $\mathcal V(P)$ of strict inverse sequences. Let $B(P)=\prod_nV(P)_n$ and $u=1-s$ with $\operatorname{pr}_n s=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$ as in [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Define $F(P)=\operatorname{mappingCocone}(-u)$, the principal specialization of the intrinsic fiber of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Its degree-$i$ coordinates are $(x,y)\in B(P)^i\oplus B(P)^{i-1}$ and its differential is $(d x,u x-d y)$. For every $P$ define the standard total-tensor right unitor $T_P(R_W[0])\cong P$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and define $v_n:P\to V(P)_n$ by its inverse followed by $1_P\otimes\iota_n$, where $\iota_n:R_W[0]\to[R_W\xrightarrow{t^{n+1}}R_W]$ is the degree-zero cone inclusion. For a chain map $\eta:P\to F(P)$ define UnitFormula to mean that its first projection is the product lift of the actual maps $v_n$ and that its second, degree-minus-one component is zero in every integer degree. Thus UnitFormula specifies precisely the coordinates $( (v_n)_n,0)$; it does not assert existence of a chain map. No flatness or boundedness restriction is used in these constructions, and the coefficient and scheme universes remain independent.
